        "target": "did:web:my-client.example.org",
        "names": ["admin", "editor"]
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
- name: target-role-mapper
  protocol: oid4vc
  protocolMapper: oid4vc-target-role-mapper
  config:
    claim.name: roles
    clientId: did:web:my-client.example.org

Warning

KC 26.4+ does not allow two oid4vc-target-role-mapper mappers with the same claim.name in the same scope (the realm import will fail with Duplicate key [credentialSubject, roles]). Pick one target per VC, or use distinct claim names. Note that the FIWARE vcverifier and the chart's ODRL/OPA helpers look for credentialSubject.roles[*].target by default, so deviating from the roles claim name requires a matching policy update.

docs.title: oid4vc-static-claim-mapper
docs.text:
Name: Static Claim Mapper

Allows setting a hardcoded / static value on any property of the credentialSubject. Useful for adding fixed metadata that doesn't vary per user, such as a schema version, an issuer-side identifier or a fixed membership type.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Label Type Default Description claim.name Static Claim Property Name String — The property name to set the static value on. staticValue Static Claim Value String — Value to be set for the property.

docs.title: Example output
docs.text:
{
  "credentialSubject": {
    "schemaVersion": "1.0"
  }
}

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
- name: static-claim-mapper
  protocol: oid4vc
  protocolMapper: oid4vc-static-claim-mapper
  config:
    claim.name: schemaVersion
    staticValue: "1.0"

docs.title: oid4vc-issued-at-time-claim-mapper
docs.text:
Name: Issuance Date Claim Mapper

Sets the issuance date/time claim in the credential subject. Supports truncation to larger time units to prevent user correlation based on precise timestamps — a useful privacy measure.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Property Label Type Default Description claim.name Time Claim Name String iat The property name for the issuance time claim. truncateToTimeUnit Truncate To Time Unit List — Truncate time to the first second of the chosen unit. Such as to prevent correlation of credentials based on this time value. valueSource Source of Value List COMPUTE Tells the protocol mapper where to get the information.

docs.title: truncateToTimeUnit options
docs.text: Value Description MINUTES Truncate to the start of the current minute HOURS Truncate to the start of the current hour HALF_DAYS Truncate to the start of the current half-day DAYS Truncate to the start of the current day WEEKS Truncate to the start of the current week MONTHS Truncate to the start of the current month YEARS Truncate to the start of the current year

docs.title: valueSource options
docs.text: Value Description COMPUTE (default) Keycloak computes the current time in seconds at issuance. VC Reads the time from the Verifiable Credential's own issuanceDate field.

docs.title: Example output
docs.text:
{
  "credentialSubject": {
    "iat": 1713916800
  }
}

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
- name: issued-at-time-mapper
  protocol: oid4vc
  protocolMapper: oid4vc-issued-at-time-claim-mapper
  config:
    claim.name: iat
    valueSource: COMPUTE
    truncateToTimeUnit: HOURS

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text: Mapper ID Purpose oid4vc-context-mapper Add @context URL(s) to the credential oid4vc-subject-id-mapper Set the subject id from a chosen user attribute oid4vc-generated-id-mapper Always generate a new random subject id oid4vc-user-attribute-mapper Map user profile attributes to the subject oid4vc-target-role-mapper Map client roles (per clientId) to the subject oid4vc-static-claim-mapper Set a hardcoded value on any subject property oid4vc-issued-at-time-claim-mapper Set the issuance timestamp (with optional truncation) ~~oid4vc-vc-type-mapper~~ Deprecated in 26.4+ — use the scope attribute vc.verifiable_credential_type instead

docs.title: Release 10.x.x
docs.text:
Version 10.x.x of the Data Space Connector contains a major change to the Keycloak deployment and to the OID4VCI realm model. They will be listed below, together with required actions for migration.

The two drivers of this release are:

  1. The Bitnami Keycloak Helm chart was withdrawn, so the umbrella now depends on the CloudPirates Keycloak chart. The CloudPirates chart targets the upstream Quarkus image (quay.io/keycloak/keycloak) and exposes a different values.yaml shape than Bitnami's, so the entire keycloak: configuration block must be rewritten.
  2. Keycloak 26.4 redesigned OID4VCI (keycloak/keycloak#39768). The realm-attribute scheme vc.<name>.* and the components.CredentialBuilder block are gone; per-credential configuration moved to ClientScope attributes on scopes with protocol: "oid4vc", and several mapper config keys were renamed or removed. The DSC chart's realm.verifiableCredentials API has been adjusted accordingly.

docs.title: 10.22.0 — APISIX upgraded to chart v3
docs.text:
• decentralized-iam bumped to 3.0.0, which brings odrl-authorization 3.0.0 and with it the APISIX sub-chart's major upgrade from chart 2.x to v3. The APISIX gateway app version is unaffected; only the APISIX chart's own contract changes. This chart's values keep working: the DSC only sets decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix to disable the ingress controller, disable etcd and scrape Prometheus — none of those keys changed.
  • No default Admin API key anymore. APISIX chart v3 stops shipping the public default admin keys and generates a random one into a Secret instead. On a fresh install (the local k3s deployment and any new release) this is transparent — nothing to do. On an in-place helm upgrade of an existing release the chart preserves the key via lookup, but the upgrade must run with Helm 3.8+ and must not use --reuse-values (re-pass the full values, or use --reset-then-reuse-values on Helm 3.14+). GitOps/helm template renders without cluster access should pin a key with decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix.apisix.admin.credentials.secretName.
  • See the odrl-authorization 3.0.0 release note for the full APISIX migration details.

docs.title: 10.21.0 — Marketplace on the Business API Ecosystem 2026.10.20 release
docs.text:
• The marketplace runs the components of the Business API Ecosystem release 2026.10.20. The business-api-ecosystem subchart was bumped to 1.3.1, which deploys the logic proxy 11.25.3 (was 11.20.3) and the charging backend 11.9.1 (was 11.7.0). Both only add optional settings: existing values keep working.
  • The logic proxy builds the user's profile from the credential (it needs 11.22.0 or later). If your values pin marketplace.bizEcosystemLogicProxy.statefulset.image.tag to an older version, as the local marketplace guide suggested, remove the pin.
  • The charging backend can be auto-instrumented. It now runs Python 3.9, and the chart gives it the Django settings its instrumentation loads before the application starts. Annotate it with instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-python: "true" in marketplace.bizEcosystemChargingBackend.deployment.additionalAnnotations (see Observability).
  • Python auto-instrumentation exports its spans. The Python agent of the OpenTelemetry Operator ships no gRPC exporter, but the Instrumentation set gRPC for every language, so injected Python workloads exported nothing. Python now uses OTLP/HTTP, by default to port 4318 of the bundled collector; set tracing.autoInstrumentation.python.endpoint if you export to another collector. Java and Node.js keep gRPC.
  • The default Python agent is 0.61b0 (was 0.62b1). 0.62b1 bundles a urllib3 that needs Python 3.10, and broke the start of Python 3.9 workloads such as the charging backend.

The charging backend keeps its data in MongoDB: the new version adds collections and fields, and existing data needs no migration.

docs.title: 10.20.7 — Reference profiles
docs.text:
• Reference profiles to start a real deployment from. charts/data-space-connector/examples/ has example values files for a provider (provider.yaml, plus provider-marketplace.yaml for the provider's own local marketplace, not the Central Marketplace) and a consumer (consumer.yaml), and charts/trust-anchor/examples/ one for the trust anchor, to adapt to your installation. Their README lists the prerequisites, the placeholders to replace, the Secrets to create and the installation steps.

The charts do not change. No migration is required.

docs.title: 10.20.2 — Configurable database name and port for Scorpio
docs.text:
• The Scorpio broker can now be pointed at a database with a non-default name and port. The scorpio-broker-aaio subchart was bumped to 0.6.0, which adds scorpio.db.name and scorpio.db.port. Both are empty by default, so Scorpio keeps using its built-in defaults (database ngb on port 5432) and the rendered manifests do not change. Set them to connect Scorpio to a differently named database or a non-standard port.

No migration is required.

docs.title: 10.20.1 — Upgrades with cert-manager, and auto-instrumentation on a first install
docs.text:
• Upgrading a release with cert-manager.enabled no longer hangs. The chart runs cert-manager's startupapicheck job on every upgrade, but its service account, Role and RoleBinding were only created on install and deleted afterwards. On an upgrade the job could not start its pod (serviceaccount "<release>-cert-manager-startupapicheck" not found), and helm upgrade waited until it timed out (post-upgrade hooks failed: ... startupapicheck not ready). They are now created again on every upgrade.
  • Auto-instrumentation installs at the first attempt. With tracing.autoInstrumentation.enabled and the opentelemetry-operator subchart in the same release, a first helm install failed with resource mapping not found ... kind "Instrumentation", since the operator's chart installs that CRD as a template. The Instrumentation is now a post-install/post-upgrade hook: a new <release>-otel-webhook-wait job waits for the operator's webhook, then the Instrumentation is created, and then the annotated pods are restarted, as before.
  • The default Python agent (tracing.autoInstrumentation.python.image) was autoinstrumentation-python:0.54b0, which is no longer published: a pod annotated for Python injection stayed in ImagePullBackOff, and its rollout never finished. It is now 0.62b1, the last one that supports Python 3.9 (later ones require 3.10). The marketplace charging backend runs Python 3.9 from 11.8.3 on; the 11.7.0 that the marketplace chart deploys runs Python 3.8, which no published agent supports, so do not annotate it for injection.

The local environment in k3s/ gets its monitoring and gaia-x scenarios working again. The monitoring profile lost the provider's environment variables of contract management and the marketplace, and the gx-registry never started. The provider profile now sets the logic proxy's purchase and SIOP client through purchaseEnabled and siop.clientId instead of additionalEnvVars. The chart already renders those two variables, and the duplicates made an upgrade fail with The order in patch list doesn't match $setElementOrder list.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
On the upgrade, Helm removes the Instrumentation from the release and the new hook creates it again; the annotated pods are restarted with the agent, as on every upgrade. From then on it is a hook resource:

  • helm uninstall no longer deletes it. Remove it afterwards with kubectl delete instrumentation -n <namespace> <release>-auto-instrumentation.
  • To roll back to an earlier version, delete it first: an earlier version manages it as a regular resource and refuses to take over one it did not create (invalid ownership metadata).

docs.title: 10.20.0 — The chart's MongoDB runs as a service account of its own
docs.text:
The pods of the MongoDB that the chart deploys (managedMongo) ran as the operator's mongodb-database service account. The operator's chart creates it in a single namespace only (its database.namespace), so a connector in any other namespace had to create it by hand, and its MongoDB stayed Pending without it (serviceaccounts "mongodb-database" not found).

The chart now creates a service account of its own, <release>-mongodb, with the same Role and RoleBinding, and runs the MongoDB pods as it (managedMongo.serviceAccount). Under another name it never collides with the operator's, wherever that is created.

  • managedMongo.serviceAccount.name changes its name.
  • managedMongo.serviceAccount.create: false with a name runs the pods as a service account you manage yourself; without a name, as the operator's mongodb-database, as before.
  • A serviceAccountName set in managedMongo.spec.statefulSet still wins.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
The operator updates the MongoDB StatefulSet to the new service account, so its pod restarts once during helm upgrade. With the default single member, the marketplace loses its database for that restart; the data stays in the volume.

The operator's mongodb-database in the connector's namespace is no longer used. If you created it by hand, you can delete it:

kubectl delete rolebinding,role,serviceaccount -n <namespace> mongodb-database

If the operator's chart created it (database.namespace set to the connector's namespace), leave it or drop that setting from the operator's release.

docs.title: 10.19.0 — No unused users in the managed PostgreSQL
docs.text:
The PostgreSQL that the chart deploys with decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.managedPostgres no longer gets these users, which nothing connected with:

  • admin, a superuser with createdb;
  • issuer, with its issuer database.

The managed PostgreSQL of the trust-anchor chart (managedPostgres) no longer gets its admin superuser either. Each component keeps its own user and database (til, ccs, pap, keycloak, and ih for the IdentityHub), and the operator still creates its own postgres superuser.

decentralized-iam 2.3.0 brings vc-authentication 1.6.0, which drops admin from its defaults as well, together with credentials-config-service 2.7.1 and trusted-issuers-list 0.19.2.

Scorpio sets QUARKUS_FLYWAY_SCHEMAS=public and QUARKUS_FLYWAY_DEFAULT_SCHEMA=public by default (in scorpio.additionalEnvVars). Its migrations already name the public schema, so this changes nothing when it connects as postgres. It lets Scorpio connect with the owner user of a prepared database, whose search path Flyway would otherwise read as a schema name:

decentralizedIam:
  vcAuthentication:
    managedPostgres:
      config:
        preparedDatabases:
          ngb:
            defaultUsers: true
            schemas:
              public: {}
            extensions:
              postgis: public
scorpio:
  db:
    user: ngb_owner_user
    existingSecret:
      enabled: true
      name: ngb-owner-user.postgres.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do
      key: password

A list given in scorpio.additionalEnvVars replaces the default one, so add the two variables to it if you set your own.

The profiles in k3s/ (local and test environments) now connect each component with its own user instead of postgres, and Scorpio with ngb_owner_user as above. The chart's defaults still use postgres.

docs.title: Required action: drop the unused users of an existing cluster
docs.text:
The Zalando operator does not drop the users and databases that disappear from the postgresql resource, so an existing cluster keeps them after helm upgrade. Drop them by hand, in the connector's cluster (postgres, in the release's namespace):

kubectl exec -n <namespace> postgres-0 -- psql -U postgres -c 'DROP ROLE admin;'
kubectl exec -n <namespace> postgres-0 -- psql -U postgres -c 'DROP DATABASE issuer;'
kubectl exec -n <namespace> postgres-0 -- psql -U postgres -c 'DROP ROLE issuer;'
kubectl delete secret -n <namespace> \
  admin.postgres.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do \
  issuer.postgres.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do

and in the Trust Anchor's:

kubectl exec -n <namespace> postgres-0 -- psql -U postgres -c 'DROP ROLE admin;'
kubectl delete secret -n <namespace> admin.postgres.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do

If you connected anything with one of them, keep it in managedPostgres.config.users (and databases) instead: DROP ROLE fails for a user that still owns objects.

docs.title: 10.17.0 — APISIX: a ClusterIP gateway, etcd only when used, no catch-all route
docs.text:
decentralized-iam 2.2.0 brings odrl-authorization 2.5.0, which changes three defaults of the data service gateway (all under decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix):

Value Before Now service.type NodePort ClusterIP etcd.enabled true false catchAllRoute.enabled true false
  • As a NodePort, the gateway also answered plain HTTP on a port of every node, outside of the Ingress that carries its host and TLS. It is now published through its Ingress only.
  • The default standalone mode reads the routes from a ConfigMap and never connected to etcd. That etcd ran three replicas of bitnamilegacy/etcd:latest without authentication, each on an 8Gi volume, and held APISIX back with a wait-etcd init container.
  • The catch-all route sent every unmatched path (/*) to my-broker:8080, which does not exist.

The same release brings the apisix chart 2.18.2 (APISIX 3.17.0 → 3.19.0) and odrl-pap 1.8.1.

The keys decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.opa.{enabled,resourceUrl,port,policies,methods,data} are removed: odrl-authorization never read them, and reads the OPA sidecar's settings from opa.config instead. Setting one now fails the render.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
These apply on helm upgrade:

  • Traditional mode: APISIX in a mode that reads its configuration from etcd (a mode other than standalone, unless the role is traditional with config_provider: yaml) fails to render without an etcd, naming the values to set. The upgrade stops before changing anything. Set decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix.etcd.enabled: true, or apisix.externalEtcd.host to an etcd of your own. The provider, consumer-auth and consent-trust-anchor profiles in k3s/ do the former.
  • NodePort: whatever reached the gateway on a port of the nodes has to go through its Ingress (decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix.ingress), or set decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix.service.type: NodePort.
  • Catch-all route: a deployment that used it, with its own upstream, sets decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix.catchAllRoute.enabled: true.
  • Removed OPA keys: move what was set there under decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.opa.config, or drop it; it never had an effect.

docs.title: Required action: the etcd volumes of a standalone APISIX
docs.text:
Upgrading a release that runs APISIX in the default standalone mode removes the etcd StatefulSet, but Kubernetes keeps the PersistentVolumeClaims it created, one per replica (three by default). Once the upgrade is done, delete them:

kubectl delete pvc -n <namespace> data-<release>-etcd-0 data-<release>-etcd-1 data-<release>-etcd-2

docs.title: 10.16.0 — Safer defaults for the Keycloak realm
docs.text:
The realm the chart imports by default no longer comes with a known login, nor with the password grant on its public clients, and it takes plain HTTP only from private addresses:

Value Before Now keycloak.realm.sslRequired none external: HTTPS for requests from public addresses keycloak.realm.defaultClients.account-console.directAccessGrantsEnabled true false keycloak.realm.defaultClients.admin-cli.directAccessGrantsEnabled true false keycloak.realm.users admin-user, password test none keycloak.realm.clientRoles ADMIN on the connector's own client (${DID}) none

In a deployment that did not replace them, anyone could log in as admin-user with the password in this repository and get a credential with the ADMIN role, issued by the organisation; with the password grant on the public clients, a single request to the token endpoint was enough. A map of client roles was merged into the default one, so the ADMIN role also reached deployments that declared their own roles as a map.

Besides, a default client set to null (keycloak.realm.defaultClients.admin-cli: null) is now left out of the realm; it failed the render before. See Keycloak.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
Keycloak imports the realm only when it does not exist, so an existing realm does not change. The new defaults apply to realms created from now on, including a reinstallation.

  • Users and client roles: a deployment that relied on admin-user or on the ADMIN role of the defaults declares them in keycloak.realm.users and keycloak.realm.clientRoles.
  • Password grant: whatever logs in with a user's password through account-console or admin-cli fails with unauthorized_client. People log in through the browser or get their credentials with a wallet; components use a confidential client of their own with the client credentials grant, as the vc-operator does (vcCredentials). The credentials helper that logged in this way is no longer part of the chart; the Central Marketplace guide shows its replacement. To turn the grant back on for one client:
keycloak:
  realm:
    defaultClients:
      account-console:
        directAccessGrantsEnabled: true

The k3s profiles do this, because the integration tests and doc/scripts/get_credential.sh use it. - HTTPS: a realm whose frontend URL (keycloak.realm.frontendURL) is plain HTTP answers HTTPS required to requests from public addresses. Calls from private addresses, such as the components inside the cluster calling http://<release>-keycloak:8080, keep working. Keycloak takes the client address from the X-Forwarded-For header of the ingress, and the scheme from the frontend URL, so a realm with an https frontend URL is not affected; refusing plain HTTP there is up to the ingress. To go back to accepting HTTP from anywhere, set keycloak.realm.sslRequired: none.

docs.title: Required action: existing realms
docs.text:
An existing realm keeps admin-user and its password. Unless it is deliberately in use, delete the user, or at least change its password, in the Keycloak admin console (realm, Users). The other settings can be applied there too:

  • Realm settings → General → Require SSL: external requests;
  • Clients → account-console and admin-cli → Capability config: clear Direct access grants.

docs.title: 10.15.1 — OID4VP clients accept the verifier's own state
docs.text:
Since 6.24.2, the VCVerifier puts its own session id in the state of the authorization request, instead of echoing the one the client sent. oid4vp-client-lib up to 0.0.6 rejected that request with Authorization request contains wrong state., so with the VCVerifier 6.27.0 of 10.15.0 no component that authenticates through the library could obtain an access token from a verifier. That broke the OID4VC contract negotiation of fdsc-edc, the order processing of contract-management in a central marketplace, and the consent-facade's access to the provider's TM Forum APIs.

oid4vp-client-lib 0.0.7 no longer checks the state, and the following charts carry it:

Chart Version Image fdsc-edc 0.7.6 → 0.7.8 1.8.4 → 1.8.5 contract-management 3.6.0 → 3.6.2 3.4.0 → 3.4.1 consent-facade 0.2.0 → 0.2.1 0.0.14 → 0.4.2

The trust-anchor chart moves its own consent-facade dependency, which the authority runs, to 0.2.1 as well. No configuration changes are needed. A deployment that sets its own image tag for one of these components has to move it to the version in the table.

docs.title: 10.15.0 — The verifier's metrics move to their own port
docs.text: The VCVerifier (6.27.0, chart vcverifier 4.17.0, through vc-authentication 1.5.2 and decentralized-iam 2.1.28) now serves /metrics, and a copy of /health, on port 9090 of the verifier Service (metrics), set with decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.vcverifier.deployment.server.metricsPort. Port 3000, which the verifier's Ingress publishes, no longer answers /metrics, so the metrics are not reachable from outside the cluster any more. /metrics also counts the requests to the API now; before, it counted none of them.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
• Anything that scraped the verifier's metrics on port 3000, or through its Ingress, has to scrape verifier:9090/metrics instead. To keep the metrics on the main port, set decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.vcverifier.deployment.server.metricsPort: 3000.

The VCVerifier goes from 6.23.1 to 6.27.0, which also:

  • accepts WebSocket upgrades only from the verifier's own origin, so a frontend on another origin can no longer open the login WebSocket;
  • makes each login session single-use;
  • verifies W3C Data Integrity proofs (ecdsa-rdfc-2019, eddsa-rdfc-2022 and the JCS suites) in JSON-LD credentials.

The same release also brings, through vc-authentication 1.5.2: credentials-config-service 2.7.0, dss-validation-service 0.1.0 and trusted-issuers-list 0.19.1. postgres-operator stays at 1.15.1.

docs.title: 10.14.0 — IdentityHub startup probe
docs.text:
IdentityHub now has a startup probe on its liveness endpoint, configured under identityhub.startupProbe and enabled by default. It gives IdentityHub up to 5 minutes to start (30 checks, every 10 seconds) before the liveness probe takes over.

Before, the liveness probe gave it about 35 seconds. When the node was busy starting the rest of the release, IdentityHub was killed before it had started and went into a restart loop, and its deployment could exceed its progress deadline. A restart in the middle of the first start could also leave the super-user with an API key other than identityhub.superuser.key: IdentityHub seeds the super-user only when it does not exist yet, so every call to the Identity API was rejected with 401 Invalid API token. To repair such a deployment, delete the super-user participant context from the IdentityHub database and restart IdentityHub.

No action is required. Set identityhub.startupProbe.enabled: false to keep the previous behaviour.

docs.title: 10.13.0 — EDC 0.18: fdsc-edc and IdentityHub move together
docs.text: fdsc-edc moves to 1.8.x (chart 0.7.x), built on Eclipse EDC 0.18.1. The DCP wire contract between the controlplane and IdentityHub changed in that range, so IdentityHub moves with it, to tractusx/identityhub:0.5.0-rc1 (EDC 0.18.0). An IdentityHub on EDC 0.14 does not work with the new controlplane. The full list of fdsc-edc changes is in its release notes.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
• The connector speaks DSP 2025/1 only. Counterparties still on DSP 2024/1 or 0.8 can no longer negotiate with it.
  • The connector calls the counterparty's /.well-known/dspace-version without a token, and serves its own without one. A PEP in front of the DSP endpoint must not require a token on that path.
  • The IdentityHub Identity API moves from /api/identity/v1alpha to /api/identity/v1beta, and its {participantContextId} path segment is the participant id URL-encoded once (did%3Aweb%3Amp-operations.org), no longer base64url. The participant creation payload carries participantContextId instead of participantId. The chart's bootstrap, rotation and credential-sync Jobs are updated; scripts of your own that call the Identity API must follow.
  • IdentityHub needs one more datasource, participantcontextconfig, on the same database as the others. The chart configures it.
  • The log formatter class of the IdentityHub image is now org.eclipse.tractusx.monitor.formatter.ColorfulFormatter. Values that override identityhub.logging with the old org.eclipse.tractusx.identityhub.monitor.ColorfulFormatter must be renamed.

docs.title: Required action: existing IdentityHub deployments
docs.text:
IdentityHub migrates its database by itself on start. Back up the database and the vault first: going back means restoring both.

IdentityHub's migrations do not carry existing rows forward, so an upgraded deployment starts, reports healthy and is unusable. Four tables are affected, and they surface one at a time — each fix only reveals the next — so run all four statements in one go, after the first start on the new image. Tracked upstream as tractusx-identityhub#371.

-- 1. participant contexts have no configuration row: every authenticated Identity API call
--    returns 500 with `No configuration found for participant context super-user`
INSERT INTO edc_participant_context_config
  (participant_context_id, created_date, last_modified_date, entries, private_entries)
SELECT participant_context_id,
       (extract(epoch from now())*1000)::bigint,
       (extract(epoch from now())*1000)::bigint,
       '{}', '{}'
FROM participant_context
ON CONFLICT (participant_context_id) DO NOTHING;

-- 2. STS clients are not linked to their participant context (column defaults to ''):
--    POST /api/sts/token returns 500 with the same exception and an EMPTY context id
UPDATE edc_sts_client SET participant_context_id = id WHERE participant_context_id = '';

-- 3. key pairs have no usage (column defaults to '', but it holds a JSON array):
--    `MismatchedInputException: No content to map due to end-of-input` in SqlKeyPairResourceStore
UPDATE keypair_resource SET usage = '["sign_token","sign_presentation"]'
 WHERE usage = '' OR usage IS NULL;

-- 4. credential usage default is lower-case, the enum constant is not:
--    `No enum constant CredentialUsage.holder`
UPDATE credential_resource SET usage = 'Holder' WHERE usage = 'holder';
ALTER TABLE credential_resource ALTER COLUMN usage SET DEFAULT 'Holder';

Empty entries in (1) is enough; the row only has to exist. The bootstrap Job retries on its own and completes once (1) and (2) are in place.

Then the DID document: it keeps the CredentialService endpoint it was published with, which carries the participant id in base64url. The bootstrap Job does not rewrite it for a participant that already exists, so every DCP presentation query against it returns 404 (Object of type IdentityHubParticipantContext with ID=<base64> was not found) and the counterparty reports a bare 401. Either start IdentityHub on an empty database and vault, so the bootstrap Job registers the participant again, or replace the endpoint.

PATCH is documented as the replace operation but appends on 0.5.0-rc1, leaving two entries with the same id — resolvers then pick the stale one and nothing appears to change. Delete and re-add instead (the {did} segment of both calls stays base64url, while {participantContextId} is URL-encoded):

DID=did:web:mp-operations.org
CTX=$(printf '%s' "$DID" | sed 's/:/%3A/g')
B64=$(printf '%s' "$DID" | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n')

# removes every entry with that id, including the stale one
curl -X DELETE "${IDENTITY_API}/participants/${CTX}/dids/${B64}/endpoints?serviceId=credential-service&autoPublish=false" \
  -H "x-api-key: ${SUPERUSER_API_KEY}"

curl -X POST "${IDENTITY_API}/participants/${CTX}/dids/${B64}/endpoints?autoPublish=true" \
  -H "x-api-key: ${SUPERUSER_API_KEY}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"id\":\"credential-service\",\"type\":\"CredentialService\",\"serviceEndpoint\":\"${CREDENTIAL_SERVICE_URL}/api/credentials/v1/participants/${CTX}\"}"

Verify the published document ends up with exactly one credential-service entry, and that the verification method still carries the same public key it had before the upgrade — if the key changed, the bootstrap re-derived an identity and every counterparty's trust list is now stale.

docs.title: 10.12.0 — the chart's own values are validated
docs.text: Helm used to accept any key in the values and ignore the ones nothing reads, so a typo, a renamed value or one that no longer exists was silently dropped and the release came up without it. The chart now ships a values.schema.json, and Helm validates the values against it on install, upgrade, template and lint.

docs.title: What is validated
docs.text: Values Validated by This chart's own keys (registration, identityhub, rainbow, statusListServer, vcCredentials, elsi, tracing, dataSpaceConfig, managedMongo, certManagerResources, consentManagement, issuance, extraManifests, nameOverride, fullnameOverride, imagePullSecrets) this chart's schema: unknown keys and wrong types are refused Free-form maps under them (annotations, labels, node selectors, affinities, resources, security contexts, env maps, identityhub.customCaCerts, managedMongo.spec, tracing.resourceAttributes) not validated: they take any key A subchart's key (keycloak, decentralizedIam, tm-forum-api, vault, marketplace, scorpio, ...) the subchart's own schema, if it ships one scorpio.ccs, tm-forum-api.registration (removed in 10.11.0) refused with a message naming their replacement

docs.title: Required action: remove keys the chart does not know
docs.text:
A values file with a key this chart does not declare no longer renders:

Error: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
data-space-connector:
- at '/registration': additional properties 'tyop' not allowed

Before upgrading, render your values against the new version and fix or remove what it reports:

helm template <release> <chart> --version 10.12.0 -f <your-values.yaml> > /dev/null

Every key reported was already ignored by the previous version, so removing it does not change the deployment. Values files copied from the full values.yaml of an older release are the usual source, in particular the registrations removed in 10.11.0 (rainbow.ccs, scorpio.ccs, tm-forum-api.registration), which are refused even with enabled: false.

helm install|upgrade|template --skip-schema-validation (Helm 3.16 and later) skips the validation as a stopgap.

docs.title: Values documented
docs.text: Values the templates read but values.yaml did not list are now declared, with defaults that keep the previous behaviour: nameOverride, fullnameOverride, imagePullSecrets, elsi.keystore, identityhub.didIngress.{className,annotations,hosts,tls}, rainbow.ingress.className and vcCredentials.issuers.

docs.title: 10.11.0 — safer defaults and a single way to register services at the verifier
docs.text: A release with the umbrella's default values upgrades without any action. The breaking changes below only concern releases that use the registrations at the verifier being removed, or rainbow.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
Change Who is affected Action scorpio.ccs removed, with its scorpio-registration ConfigMap and the default scorpio.additionalVolumes entry that mounted it releases that ran the registration script from their own init container in scorpio.initContainers move the service to the verifier's registration and remove that init container - its ConfigMap is no longer rendered, so the pod would not start rainbow.ccs removed, with the register-credential-config init container of the rainbow pod releases with rainbow.ccs.enabled: true move the tpp-service to the verifier's registration tm-forum-api.registration removed, with its Job and ConfigMap releases with tm-forum-api.registration.enabled: true (the previous default) if the release relied on it, move the service to the verifier's registration - see below whether it ever registered anything contract-management.enableRainbow defaults to false releases with rainbow.enabled: true set contract-management.enableRainbow: true; the chart refuses to render rainbow without it bae-did-secret Secret removed releases that referenced it by hand nothing in the chart used it; it held a private key that was the same in every installation, so do not reuse it

Keys that are no longer read are ignored, so values files that still set them render unchanged; only the behaviour described above is gone.

docs.title: Required action: register services through the verifier
docs.text:
The umbrella had three registrations of its own at the verifier's credentials config API besides the verifier's registration Job. They are gone; every service is registered with decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.vcverifier.registration.services, which is how all the examples in k3s/ already do it. Each entry is posted as is to the /service endpoint:

decentralizedIam:
  vcAuthentication:
    vcverifier:
      registration:
        enabled: true
        services:
          - id: tmf-api                                  # was <component>.ccs.id
            defaultOidcScope: default                    # was <component>.ccs.defaultOidcScope.name
            oidcScopes:
              default:
                credentials:                             # one entry per former credentialTypes item
                  - type: VerifiableCredential
                    trustedParticipantsLists:
                      - https://tir.example.org          # was defaultOidcScope.trustedParticipantsLists
                    trustedIssuersLists:
                      - http://trusted-issuers-list:8080 # was defaultOidcScope.trustedIssuersLists

A former oidcScopes block written as a list of credentials per scope (default: [ {type: ...} ]) becomes default: {credentials: [ {type: ...} ]} - the verifier only accepts the latter.

Like the removed registrations, the Job only creates services: one that already exists is left as it is. A service registered by the old mechanism stays registered and needs no re-registration.

Whether the old registration did anything:

  • tm-forum-api.registration never registered a service with credentialTypes, the key the values have documented since 9.x: it posted a body that is not valid JSON and the Job succeeded anyway. Only a release that set ccs.oidcScopes itself, in the {credentials: [...]} shape, got a service out of it.
  • scorpio.ccs only rendered the script. Unless an init container running it was added to scorpio.initContainers, nothing was registered.
  • rainbow.ccs ran on every start of the rainbow pod.

docs.title: Rainbow integration of contract management
docs.text:
The contract-management subchart enables its rainbow integration by default, while the umbrella deploys no rainbow by default. Contract management then tried to register at a rainbow that did not exist on every start and called it on every order. The integration now follows rainbow's default:

rainbow:
  enabled: true
contract-management:
  enableRainbow: true   # required together with rainbow.enabled

docs.title: Other changes
docs.text:
These need no action:

  • APISIX gateway service: decentralizedIam.odrlAuthorization.apisix.service.externalTrafficPolicy defaults to empty, so Kubernetes applies its own default - still Cluster for NodePort and LoadBalancer - and the service can be set to ClusterIP, which the apisix chart's Cluster default made the API server reject.
  • Verifier registration deadline: decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.vcverifier.registration.job.activeDeadlineSeconds is 1200. The subchart's 300 seconds regularly ran out on a fresh install before the verifier was ready, failing the release.
  • Images: the TM Forum API proxy uses envoyproxy/envoy:distroless-v1.27.7, which is what the floating distroless-v1.27-latest resolved to. Keycloak and the status-list-server, both pinned, use imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent.
  • Trusted-issuers-list registration: unchanged in behaviour - an issuer that is already registered is left as it is. The Job now says that changes to an existing issuer in the values do not reach the list; that takes the trusted-issuers-list API.

docs.title: 10.10.0 — eIDAS 2.0 validation moves into VCVerifier
docs.text:
The external dss-validation-service is no longer how eIDAS certificate chains are checked. VCVerifier validates them itself, with PKIX chain building against a trust store it builds from the EU List of Trusted Lists (ETSI TS 119 612). This release pins decentralized-iam 2.1.23 -> 2.1.25 (vcverifier subchart 4.15.3, VCVerifier 6.23.1). 10.9.0 already shipped 2.1.23, which carries the validation itself but spells the LOTL override lotUrl

Full documentation: eIDAS 2.0 Compliance. Decision record: ADR-0006.

docs.title: Off by default
docs.text:
decentralizedIam:
  vcAuthentication:
    vcverifier:
      deployment:
        eidas:
          enabled: false

An existing release upgrades to a no-op. Nothing is fetched and no credential changes behaviour until the block is switched on.

docs.title: Two mechanisms, different triggers
docs.text:
eidas.enabled builds the trust store. What then consults it depends on the issuer:

Mechanism Trigger Covers Formats did:elsi proof check iss is a did:elsi: DID x5c chain + organizationIdentifier ↔ DID match any EidasValidationService credential type carries eidasConfig.enabled: true x5c chain + per-type allowedCountries / requireQualified SD-JWT only

A did:elsi deployment gets validation from eidas.enabled alone. A did:web or HTTPS issuer does not: those resolve their key from the DID document or JWKS and the x5c header is ignored by the proof check, so without eidasConfig on an SD-JWT type the trust lists are fetched on every refresh and never consulted — with nothing failing to indicate it.

eidasConfig is also the only source of per-type country and qualified-service filters; the did:elsi path searches all countries and applies no qualified filter.

docs.title: SD-JWT only
docs.text:
EidasValidationService is implemented for dc+sd-jwt and nothing else. A jwt_vc_json credential with eidasConfig.enabled: true is rejected outright with ErrorEidasSDJWTRequired — not skipped. This constraint applies to that mechanism only; the did:elsi proof check works for any format.

The shipped eIDAS overlay now issues dc+sd-jwt so that both mechanisms apply, and the DCQL query matching them uses meta.vct_values (flat array) instead of meta.type_values.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text: Change Action Maven profile elsi renamed to eidas mvn clean deploy -Plocal,elsi → -Plocal,eidas. Maven does not fail on an unknown profile id, so the old invocation silently deploys without the overlay. k3s/provider-elsi.yaml deleted, k3s/consumer-elsi.yaml renamed Use k3s/provider-eidas.yaml / k3s/consumer-eidas.yaml. decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.dss deprecated No effect once eidas.enabled is true. Remove it at your convenience. verifier.elsi.validationEndpoint gone Removed upstream in vcverifier 4.13.0; see the Rollback notes — reverting needs a dependency pin, not a values change.

docs.title: lotlUrl, not lotUrl
docs.text:
Up to decentralized-iam 2.1.24 the vcverifier subchart declared the LOTL override as lotUrl while the server read lotlUrl, so the subchart's own key was inert. 2.1.25 renames it, and there is no backward-compatible alias: a values file that still sets

decentralizedIam:
  vcAuthentication:
    vcverifier:
      deployment:
        eidas:
          lotUrl: "https://..."     # no longer a thing

is silently ignored and the verifier falls back to the official EU LOTL. Rename it to lotlUrl. Deployments that already worked around this by setting lotlUrl need no change.

docs.title: Chart-side detail: jades.enabled is not a vc. attribute
docs.text: dsc.vcClientScopes prefixes every credential attribute with vc., which is right for Keycloak's CredentialScopeModel but wrong for jades.enabled — the keycloak-jades-vc-issuer plugin reads that one raw via clientScope.getAttribute("jades.enabled"). The template now keeps a small pass-through list, dsc.vcScopeUnprefixedAttributes, so the documented override actually reaches the plugin. Before this, setting jades.enabled had no effect at all.

docs.title: 10.8.0 — policies on the ServiceSpecifications a product is composed of
docs.text: contract-management can now read the ODRL policies and the credential configuration from the ServiceSpecifications a ProductSpecification is composed of, instead of only from the ProductSpecification itself. An access policy protects an API, and an API is a ServiceSpecification - so a provider composing one product out of three services can author three policies where they belong, and an order for that product activates all of them.

docs.title: Off by default
docs.text:
contract-management:
  enableSpecificationComposition: false
  specificationCompositionMaxDepth: 2

Enabling it changes which configuration an order activates, so it is opt-in per deployment. It also adds one TMForum read per referenced ServiceSpecification to the activation of an order.

docs.title: What it does when enabled
docs.text: Levels read the ordered ProductSpecification, the ServiceSpecifications it references, and recursively the ProductSpecifications it bundles. ResourceSpecifications are not read - they carry no connector configuration. Aggregation union, per level. Policies are de-duplicated by odrl:uid, credential configurations by value. Two different policies claiming one odrl:uid fail the activation, because the ODRL-PAP keys an installed policy by that uid. Credentials widen the trusted-issuers-list evaluates several configurations of one credential type as an OR, so a permissive part relaxes a restrictive one. Author with that in mind. One provider a composition that declares more than one provider fails the activation. A part that declares none inherits the composition's provider. Depth specificationCompositionMaxDepth levels; a deeper or cyclic composition is truncated and logged with a warning naming the specification, the skipped references and the limit. Broken references a referenced offering, specification, quote or provider that cannot be read now fails the activation with a logged error instead of activating nothing silently.

docs.title: Fixed regardless of the flag
docs.text:
Three ways a flat order could already fail are gone:

  • a ProductSpecification without any productSpecCharacteristic, or a characteristic without a valueType, raised a NullPointerException and took the whole order's activation down;
  • an offering that bundles others instead of referencing a specification failed the activation of every other item in the same order;
  • an order that legitimately configures nothing resolved to nothing at all, which the notification listener answered with a 404, which made the TMForum hub redeliver the event.

docs.title: Component versions
docs.text:
Component Version Why contract-management chart 3.5.36 (app 3.3.12) reads the composed specifications and grants credentials under the id of the order that granted them trusted-issuers-list app 0.9.1 the scope-addressed credential endpoints. 0.9.0 carries the API but does not start against MySQL, so 0.9.1 is the first usable release

Both are delivered by the chart chain: decentralized-iam 2.1.21 brings trusted-issuers-list app 0.9.1 through vc-authentication 1.3.7, and the umbrella depends on decentralized-iam 2.1.22. No image override is needed.

docs.title: Behaviour change outside the flag
docs.text: A single ProductSpecification that declares two different parties in the provider role now fails the activation instead of picking one of them arbitrarily. Which contract-management is responsible was never defined for that shape; refusing to guess is the safer reading. Check for specifications with more than one relatedParty in the role configured as contract-management.organization.provider.role before enabling.

docs.title: 10.4.0 — upstream Keycloak 26.7.0 and the realm-scoped keystore directory
docs.text:
The umbrella bumps the CloudPirates Keycloak chart from 0.21.7 to 0.21.19 and drops the keycloak.image override entirely, so the deployment now runs the chart default — upstream docker.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.0 — instead of the SEAMWARE-patched quay.io/seamware/keycloak:26.6.3.

Removed (≤ 10.3.x) New (10.4.0) Chart cloudpirates/keycloak 0.21.7 Chart cloudpirates/keycloak 0.21.19 Image quay.io/seamware/keycloak:26.6.3 (chart-level override) Image docker.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.0 (chart default, no override) Keystore anywhere on the filesystem (e.g. /did-material/cert.pfx) Keystore under /opt/keycloak/data/<realm-name>/

The SEAMWARE fork existed only to carry the OID4VCI QR-endpoint fix (keycloak/keycloak#44623) and the Liquibase changeset 26.7.0-verifiable-credential. Both are upstream in 26.7.0, so the fork is no longer needed and is no longer published as part of this chart.

docs.title: Required action: move the PKCS12 keystore under data/<realm-name>
docs.text:
Since Keycloak 26.6.4 the java-keystore realm key provider may only read keystores from a directory named after the realm, inside a fixed keystores root — by default ${kc.home.dir}/data, which is /opt/keycloak/data on the official image. For a realm called test-realm, every keystore must live under /opt/keycloak/data/test-realm. Keystores outside that boundary keep working for a read-only startup, but any create or update on the key provider fails. See the Keycloak upgrading guide (26.6.4 migration notes).

Update the Keycloak container's mount and the storePath so both point inside the realm folder:

keycloak:
  extraVolumeMounts:
    # directory name MUST equal keycloak.realm.name
    - mountPath: /opt/keycloak/data/test-realm      # was: /did-material
      name: did-material
    - mountPath: /opt/keycloak/data/import
      name: realms
  signingKey:
    storePath: /opt/keycloak/data/test-realm/cert.pfx   # was: /did-material/cert.pfx

The init container that builds the keystore can keep writing to its own mount of the same emptyDir (/did-material) — only the Keycloak container's view of the file is constrained.

If you use a did:elsi issuer, apply the same move to the ELSI keystore:

elsi:
  storePath: /opt/keycloak/data/test-realm/keystore.p12   # was: /trust-store/keystore.p12

Deployments that set neither elsi nor keycloak.signingKey rely on the chart's fallback signing key; its default keystore path now renders as /opt/keycloak/data/{{ .Values.keycloak.realm.name }}/cert.pfx, so only the mount path needs adjusting.

The keystores root can also be relocated with the provider option --spi-keys--java-keystore--keystores-path, but the DSC chart does not set it.

docs.title: Required action: manual DB migration when upgrading from 26.6.3
docs.text:
If your database was previously running the SEAMWARE-patched quay.io/seamware/keycloak:26.6.3 image, the upgrade to upstream 26.7.0 does not apply cleanly through Liquibase: 26.6.3 already carried early, differently-named versions of the user_ver_credential / issued_ver_credential schema changes that upstream 26.7.0 introduces under its own changeset ids, so the changeset checksums no longer match on startup.

You must run the script at doc/scripts/migration_26.6.3_to_26.7.0.sql against that database to bring its 26.6.3 schema in line with what 26.7.0 expects (column renames/type changes on user_ver_credential and issued_ver_credential, the cluster_event composite primary key, and resetting the affected databasechangelog checksums so Liquibase accepts them as already applied).

Take a backup of the Keycloak database before running this script. It alters constraints and column types in place; if it fails partway through, restoring from backup is the only way back to a consistent state. Run it once, directly against the Keycloak database, before starting Keycloak on the 26.7.0 image.

This step only applies if you are coming from 26.6.3 — deployments already on 26.7.0 (or a fresh install) must not run it.

docs.title: Keycloak chart migration: Bitnami → CloudPirates
docs.text:
Removed (9.x) New (10.x) Chart oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/keycloak 25.2.0 Chart oci://registry-1.docker.io/cloudpirates/keycloak 0.21.4 Image bitnamilegacy/keycloak Image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.6.2 (upstream Quarkus) Realm import path /opt/bitnami/keycloak/data/import Realm import path /opt/keycloak/data/import Bitnami helper env vars (KEYCLOAK_EXTRA_ARGS, …) Native CLI flags via keycloak.extraArgs and feature flags

Required action:

The CloudPirates chart does not honour any Bitnami-only key. Apply the renames in the next section to your keycloak: value override and remove the keys listed afterwards.

docs.title: Required values renames in keycloak:
docs.text:
Removed (9.x) New location (10.x) keycloak.auth.adminUser keycloak.keycloak.adminUser keycloak.auth.existingSecret keycloak.keycloak.existingSecret keycloak.auth.passwordSecretKey keycloak.keycloak.secretKeys.adminPasswordKey keycloak.proxyHeaders keycloak.keycloak.proxyHeaders keycloak.service.ports.http keycloak.service.httpPort keycloak.postgresql.enabled keycloak.postgres.enabled keycloak.externalDatabase.host keycloak.database.host keycloak.externalDatabase.database keycloak.database.name keycloak.externalDatabase.user keycloak.database.username keycloak.externalDatabase.existingSecret keycloak.database.existingSecret keycloak.externalDatabase.existingSecretPasswordKey keycloak.database.secretKeys.passwordKey keycloak.initContainers keycloak.extraInitContainers keycloak.ingress.hostname keycloak.ingress.hosts[0].host keycloak.ingress.extraTls merged into keycloak.ingress.tls (single list) keycloak.ingress.pathType keycloak.ingress.hosts[0].paths[0].pathType

If your external Postgres secret carries the username under a key other than db-username (for instance the Zalando postgres-operator writes username), you also need:

keycloak:
  database:
    secretKeys:
      usernameKey: username

The following keys are no longer valid and must be removed:

keycloak.kubeVersion
keycloak.global.security.allowInsecureImages
keycloak.image.repository           # default is keycloak/keycloak; override only if you really need a custom image
keycloak.containerSecurityContext.enabled
keycloak.proxy                      # use keycloak.keycloak.proxyHeaders + TLS terminated at the ingress
keycloak.service.extraPorts         # the management/health port is exposed via metrics.enabled (see below)
keycloak.extraEnvVars:
  - KEYCLOAK_EXTRA_ARGS             # Bitnami-only; the umbrella adds --import-realm via realm.import: true
  - KC_FEATURES                     # use keycloak.features.enabled instead
  - KC_HEALTH_ENABLED               # auto-enabled by any active probe
  - KC_ADMIN_PASSWORD               # handled by keycloak.keycloak.existingSecret

docs.title: Management / health port (9000)
docs.text:
The CloudPirates chart does not expose port 9000 on the main Service. With metrics.enabled: true (the umbrella default in 10.x) it is published on a separate Service named <release>-keycloak-metrics:9000.

Required action:

If you maintain a wait-for-keycloak initContainer or any custom probe targeting <release>-keycloak:9000/health/ready, change the host to <release>-keycloak-metrics:9000.

docs.title: Default account-console client must opt into OID4VCI
docs.text:
KC 26.4+ rejects calls to /protocol/oid4vc/create-credential-offer whose bearer token is issued to a client without oid4vci.enabled=true. Many wallet flows authenticate the user via the built-in account-console client; the umbrella therefore declares the attribute on that client by default:

keycloak:
  realm:
    defaultClients:
      account-console:
        attributes:
          oid4vci.enabled: "true"

If you override defaultClients, preserve this attribute.

docs.title: OID4VCI realm model rewrite
docs.text:
The realm-attribute scheme realm.attributes vc.<name>.* and the components.CredentialBuilder block are no longer recognised by KC 26.4+. Per-credential configuration is now declared once in realm.verifiableCredentials.<name>; the DSC chart renders one ClientScope per entry with protocol: "oid4vc" and the attributes attached to the scope itself.

Before (9.x):

keycloak:
  realm:
    attributes: |
      "vc.user-credential.format": "jwt_vc",
      "vc.user-credential.scope": "UserCredential",
      "vc.user-credential.vct": "UserCredential",
      "vc.user-credential.credential_signing_alg_values_supported": "ES256"
    credentialBuilder:
      jwt-vc-builder:
        id: jwt-vc-builder
        name: jwt_vc

After (10.x):

keycloak:
  realm:
    verifiableCredentials:
      user-credential:
        attributes:
          format: "jwt_vc_json"
          verifiable_credential_type: "UserCredential"
          credential_signing_alg: "ES256"
          credential_build_config.token_jws_type: "JWT"
        protocolMappers:
          - name: context-mapper
            protocol: oid4vc
            protocolMapper: oid4vc-context-mapper
            config:
              context: https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1
          - name: email-mapper
            protocol: oid4vc
            protocolMapper: oid4vc-user-attribute-mapper
            config:
              claim.name: email
              userAttribute: email

The key under verifiableCredentials (user-credential above) is the ClientScope name — i.e. the value the wallet sends as credential_configuration_id. The realm-level realm.credentialBuilder: block is removed entirely (in KC 26.4+ credential builders are loaded via SPI service-loader, not declared per realm).

docs.title: Format strings rename
docs.text:
Format 9.x value 10.x value SD-JWT VC vc+sd-jwt dc+sd-jwt JWT-VC JSON jwt_vc jwt_vc_json

The source of truth is core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/VCFormat.java in the Keycloak repository. The same rename applies wherever the format string appears: verifiableCredentials.<name>.attributes.format, DCQL queries (realm.verifiableCredentials.<name>.protocolMappers configs that reference a format, and any DCQL configuration in decentralizedIam.vcAuthentication.credentials-config-service.registration.services[].oidcScopes.*.dcql.credentials[].format).

docs.title: Template auto-derivations (DSC chart)
docs.text:
The DSC _realm.tpl template fills in two ClientScope attributes when they are not set explicitly:

  • vc.issuer_did — derived from elsi.did if elsi.enabled: true, else from keycloak.issuerDid, else ${DID}. Sets the iss claim of every issued JWT VC.
  • vc.supported_credential_types — defaults to the value of vc.verifiable_credential_type. Drives the type array of JWT-VC JSON credentials and the metadata credential_definition.type. Override it explicitly under attributes if you need a different value than the SD-JWT vct.

docs.title: Mapper config renames
docs.text:
Mapper Old key (9.x) New key (10.x) every mapper supportedCredentialTypes (removed; mapper membership is structural per scope) oid4vc-user-attribute-mapper, oid4vc-target-role-mapper, oid4vc-static-claim-mapper, oid4vc-generated-id-mapper, oid4vc-issued-at-time-claim-mapper subjectProperty claim.name oid4vc-subject-id-mapper subjectIdProperty claim.name (plus userAttribute) oid4vc-vc-type-mapper (whole mapper) deprecated; set the scope attribute vc.verifiable_credential_type instead

A mapper that previously listed several credential types in supportedCredentialTypes must now be declared once under each VC entry it should apply to. The mapper name must be unique within a single VC's protocolMappers list — suffixing the name with the VC key (-uc, -lpc, -oc, …) makes greps easier.

KC 26.4+ does not allow two oid4vc-target-role-mapper mappers with the same claim.name in the same scope. Pick one target per VC, or use distinct claim names — but be aware that downstream verifiers (FIWARE vcverifier, ODRL/OPA in this chart) look for credentialSubject.roles[*].target by default, so deviating from the roles claim name requires a matching policy update.

docs.title: SD-JWT red list
docs.text:
KC 26.4+ enforces a "red list" of standard claims that must not be undisclosed in a SD-JWT VC: iss, iat, nbf, exp, cnf, vct, status (source: core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/sdjwt/DisclosureRedList.java).

If you override verifiableCredentials.<name>.attributes.credential_build_config.sd_jwt.visible_claims, include those seven names alongside your domain-specific ones, otherwise issuance fails with IllegalArgumentException: UndisclosedClaims contains red listed claim names.

keycloak:
  realm:
    verifiableCredentials:
      user-sd:
        attributes:
          format: "dc+sd-jwt"
          verifiable_credential_type: "LegalPersonCredential"
          credential_build_config.sd_jwt.visible_claims: "iss,iat,nbf,exp,cnf,vct,status,roles,email"

docs.title: New feature flags
docs.text:
KC main has split the original experimental OID4VCI feature flag into one base flag plus two sub-features. All three must be enabled for the DSC's issuance flow to work:

keycloak:
  features:
    enabled:
      - oid4vc-vci
      - oid4vc-vci-preauth-code        # KC 26.4+: gates the pre-authorized_code grant
      - oid4vc-vci-rest-credential-offer  # KC main / SEAMWARE 26.6.3: gates /create-credential-offer

Without oid4vc-vci-rest-credential-offer, Keycloak answers any call to /protocol/oid4vc/create-credential-offer with 403 invalid_client: "REST credential offer functionality is not enabled". The flag is defined in Profile.Feature.OID4VC_VCI_REST_CREDENTIAL_OFFER and is consumed by OID4VCIssuerEndpoint.checkRestCredentialOfferEnabled. It landed in upstream main together with the OID4VCI QR-generation fix and is present in the patched quay.io/seamware/keycloak:26.6.3 image shipped by the umbrella, even though vanilla 26.6.2 does not carry it.

The umbrella ships these three defaults out of the box.

docs.title: Endpoint changes for custom wallets / scripts
docs.text:
If you have custom code that talks to the Keycloak OID4VCI endpoints, update it as follows:

Step Old (KC 26.3) New (KC 26.4 → 26.6.2) Newer (KC main / SEAMWARE-patched 26.6.3) Request offer URI GET /protocol/oid4vc/credential-offer-uri?credential_configuration_id=X GET /protocol/oid4vc/create-credential-offer?credential_configuration_id=X&pre_authorized=true same Build offer URL ${issuer}${nonce} ${issuer}/${nonce} same /credential body {"credential_identifier":"X","format":"jwt_vc"} {"credential_configuration_id":"X"} {"credential_identifier":"<id-from-token-response>"} /credential response {"credential":"<jwt>"} {"credentials":[{"credential":"<jwt>"}]} same credential_identifier source n/a (anything accepted) n/a must come from the authorization_details[].credential_identifiers array returned by /token after exchanging the pre-authorized code

The pre_authorized query parameter on /create-credential-offer defaults to false, so it must be set explicitly to obtain the pre-authorized_code grant. The format field of /credential is no longer accepted as input — format selection happens by picking a credential_configuration_id whose configured vc.format matches what the caller expects.

docs.title: credential_identifier flow (keycloak/keycloak#47404)
docs.text:
The patched 26.6.3 image arrives with the upstream rule that /credential only accepts a credential_identifier, never a credential_configuration_id. The identifier is short-lived and bound to the issued access token:

  1. Wallet exchanges the pre-authorized code at /token.
  2. /token response contains: 
    "authorization_details": [{
  "type": "openid_credential",
  "credential_configuration_id": "user-credential",
  "credential_identifiers": ["user-credential_0000"]
}]
  3. Wallet POSTs /credential with {"credential_identifier": "user-credential_0000"}.

Sending the legacy {"credential_configuration_id": "..."} body against this image returns 400 invalid_credential_request: "Credential must be requested by credential identifier from authorization_details: [...]".

The IT framework's Wallet.java was updated accordingly: it reads authorization_details off the TokenResponse model and falls back to the previous credential_configuration_id-based body when the field is absent, so it still works against older Keycloak versions.

docs.title: Client roles consistency
docs.text:
KC 26.4+ rejects user→client role assignments where the client itself does not declare the role. The realm import attempts to auto-create the missing role and, if multiple users assign it in the same batch, fails with duplicate key violates unique constraint.

Required action:

For every clientRoles.<clientId>: [...] you set on a user, declare the same role under realm.clientRoles.<clientId>. The consumer.yaml and provider.yaml example overlays in this repository show the consistent shape (REPRESENTATIVE declared on did:web:mp-operations.org, seller/admin declared on did:web:fancy-marketplace.biz).

docs.title: Per-user verifiableCredentials assignment
docs.text:
KC main (carried by the SEAMWARE-patched 26.6.3 image — see keycloak/keycloak@6ef5a79) ties /create-credential-offer to a per-user verifiableCredentials list. A user that has not been explicitly granted a credential gets:

400 invalid_credential_offer_request
"User 'X' does not have verifiable credential 'Y'."

even with a valid token and a properly configured ClientScope.

In the realm import JSON the list lives on each user entry:

{
  "username": "employee",
  "verifiableCredentials": [
    { "credentialScopeName": "user-credential" },
    { "credentialScopeName": "operator-credential" }
  ]
}

Required action:

Either set this list per user, or set the chart flag below to have the umbrella auto-assign every VC declared in the realm to every user that has not provided its own verifiableCredentials:

keycloak:
  realm:
    wallets:
      issueCredentialsToUsers: true

wallets.enabled does not need to be true for this to work — the two flags are independent. The local k3s overlays (k3s/consumer.yaml, k3s/provider.yaml) ship with issueCredentialsToUsers: true so the example deployment works out of the box; in production you usually want to declare the per-user lists explicitly instead.

docs.title: OID4VCI draft compliance
docs.text:
Keycloak 26.6.3 implements OID4VCI Draft 15. The 26.4 redesign (keycloak/keycloak#39768) explicitly aligned the credential issuance flow with Draft 15: CredentialSubject was removed from CredentialDefinition, the format field was dropped from CredentialRequest, the metadata endpoint claims structure was rewritten and the cwt proof type was removed.

Practical implications already covered above (see Endpoint changes for custom wallets / scripts, OID4VCI realm model rewrite and Format strings rename):

  • /credential request: send credential_configuration_id (no format); response is {"credentials":[…]}.
  • /credential-offer-uri is replaced by /create-credential-offer?pre_authorized=true.
  • Format strings updated: jwt_vc → jwt_vc_json, vc+sd-jwt → dc+sd-jwt.

If you maintain a custom wallet or test harness, target Draft 15 endpoints and payloads.

docs.title: Credential request/response encryption (JWE)
docs.text:
Keycloak 26.6.x advertises OID4VCI credential encryption in the issuer metadata (/.well-known/openid-credential-issuer). Two independent features are involved, and both have caused interop failures with wallets that encrypt:

Request encryption (credential_request_encryption). Advertised whenever the realm has an asymmetric encryption key — the chart ships one via the ecdh-generated key provider in keycloak.realm.defaultKeyProviders (ECDH-ES, P-256). A wallet that encrypts the /credential request must include the issuer key's kid in the JWE header; otherwise Keycloak answers 400 invalid_encryption_parameters with Request has JWT content-type but is not a valid JWE: Missing kid in JWE header. The EUDI eudi-lib-ios-openid4vci-swift omitted the kid before 0.38.3 (fixed by "add kid to header on issuance").

Response encryption (credential_response_encryption). Advertised whenever the realm has any asymmetric key — if the ecdh-generated key is removed it simply falls back to RSA-OAEP via the realm's RSA token-signing key. A wallet requesting an encrypted response must not send alg at the top level of the credential_response_encryption object: Keycloak's model only accepts {zip, enc, jwk} and otherwise fails with Unrecognized field "alg" (class CredentialResponseEncryption). eudi-lib-ios-openid4vci-swift sent the top-level alg before 0.40.0 (fixed by "Remove alg from top level").

Guidance:

  • Wallets that opt into encryption need eudi-lib-ios-openid4vci-swift ≥ 0.40.0 (carries both fixes). Lissi does not encrypt the request/response, so it is unaffected.
  • There is no realm/chart toggle to stop advertising credential_response_encryption: it is inherent to KC 26.6.x and the RSA signing key cannot be removed. Removing the ecdh-generated key provider only neutralises request encryption (the section disappears from the metadata); response encryption stays advertised but is optional (encryption_required: false), so a wallet that does not request it is unaffected.

docs.title: Wallet compatibility
docs.text:
The chart includes an opinionated wallet preset (off by default) that registers the OIDC clients required by the wallets validated against this release. The preset only configures clients — it does not declare any credential type; that remains the deployer's job under keycloak.realm.verifiableCredentials.

Wallet Platform Tested version Default clientId OIDC requirements Recommended for Lissi ID Wallet iOS 3.1.3, 3.1.4, 3.1.5 9c481dc3-2ad0-4fe0-881d-c32ad02fe0fc PKCE S256 Production Lissi ID Wallet Android 3.1.3, 3.1.4, 3.1.5 9c481dc3-2ad0-4fe0-881d-c32ad02fe0fc PKCE S256 Production EUDI Reference Wallet (forked .DEV build — app + lib) iOS — wallet-dev PAR + DPoP + PKCE S256 Development / local testing EUDI Reference Wallet (forked .DEV build — app + libs([1][2][3]) Android — wallet-dev PAR + DPoP + PKCE S256 Development / local testing

Lissi

is the recommended wallet for production deployments.

EUDI Reference Wallet — fork required. The upstream EUDI iOS app/lib does not yet implement the OID4VCI Draft 15 model that Keycloak 26.6.3 ships, so it cannot complete an issuance flow against the DSC's Keycloak out of the box. The forks linked above carry two changes that make them usable for local DSC development:

  1. The credential issuance flow is updated to the Draft 15 endpoints/payloads documented in Endpoint changes for custom wallets / scripts above.
  2. They accept self-signed TLS certificates, which is what makes them usable against a k3s cluster with cert-manager issuing self-signed certs.
  3. They pin eudi-lib-ios-openid4vci-swift ≥ 0.40.0, required for the credential request/response encryption fixes (see Credential request/response encryption (JWE) above).

Do not use the forked EUDI build in production — its self-signed-cert handling defeats the trust model. It is intended exclusively as a developer-side tool for local data space testing.

The clientId values match what each wallet looks for in the realm — override only if the wallet vendor rotates them. The defaults are defined at charts/data-space-connector/values.yaml under keycloak.realm.wallets.lissi and keycloak.realm.wallets.eudi.

Enabling the preset:

keycloak:
  realm:
    wallets:
      enabled: true
      # Optional: auto-assign every realm-declared verifiableCredentials entry to every
      # user that does not declare its own list. Useful for smoke tests, off by default.
      issueCredentialsToUsers: false

Override any leaf without redefining the whole client, for example:

keycloak:
  realm:
    wallets:
      enabled: true
      lissi:
        clientId: <your-rotated-lissi-id>

Wallets that are not in this list are not blocked — any wallet that speaks OID4VCI Draft 15 and either PKCE S256 or PAR+DPoP+PKCE S256 can be wired up by declaring the corresponding OIDC client manually in keycloak.realm.clients.

docs.title: Reusing an existing Keycloak database (USER_VER_CREDENTIAL migration)
docs.text:
The post-26.4 OID4VCI model ties /create-credential-offer to a per-user verifiableCredentials list, backed by a custom USER_VER_CREDENTIAL table. Pointing 26.6.x at a database created by an older Keycloak fails at offer time with:

ERROR: column uvce1_0.version does not exist
  at org.keycloak.protocol.oid4vc.utils.OID4VCUtil.hasVerifiableCredential

The shipped quay.io/seamware/keycloak:26.6.3 image carries the Liquibase changeset 26.7.0-verifiable-credential, which adds the missing version column on startup. Use 26.6.3 (not 26.6.2) when reusing a database.

Related: Keycloak does not re-import an already-existing realm. Changes under keycloak.realm.* do not take effect on a running realm — delete and recreate the realm (the external DB makes this safe) for the new import to apply.

docs.title: DCQL query format gotchas
docs.text:
For Credentials Config Service / VCVerifier scopes that use DCQL (oidcScopes.<scope>.dcql):

  • meta.type_values (W3C jwt_vc_json) is an array of string arrays, e.g. [["MarketplaceCredential"]] — a flat array is rejected with cannot unmarshal string into ... type_values of type []string.
  • meta.vct_values (SD-JWT dc+sd-jwt / vc+sd-jwt) is a flat array of strings, e.g. ["LegalPersonCredential"].
  • credential_sets must be a non-empty array. A nil credential_sets serialises to JSON null, which the SwiftyJSON parser in the Lissi/EUDI wallets rejects with "JSON is invalid". For dual-format offers, list both credential ids as alternatives: credential_sets: [{ options: [["lpc-dc-sd-jwt"], ["lpc-vc-sd-jwt"]], required: true }].

docs.title: StatefulSet recreation when upgrading from 9.x (Bitnami → CloudPirates)
docs.text: The Bitnami and CloudPirates keycloak charts both name the workload <release>-keycloak, but their StatefulSet specs differ in immutable fields (serviceName, selector, volumeClaimTemplates). An in-place upgrade fails with updates to statefulset spec for fields other than ... are forbidden. Delete the old StatefulSet so it is recreated — kubectl delete statefulset <release>-keycloak (the external Postgres means no data loss; the pod is stateless).

docs.title: Migration checklist
docs.text:
1. Apply the value renames in the table above to your keycloak: block; remove the listed obsolete keys.
  2. Rewrite each entry under keycloak.realm.attributes of the form vc.<name>.* as a keycloak.realm.verifiableCredentials.<name> block with attributes and protocolMappers. Drop the keycloak.realm.credentialBuilder: block entirely.
  3. Update format strings: vc+sd-jwt → dc+sd-jwt, jwt_vc → jwt_vc_json, both in the realm config and in any DCQL queries you maintain.
  4. If you override keycloak.realm.defaultClients, preserve account-console.attributes.oid4vci.enabled: "true".
  5. Add oid4vc-vci-preauth-code to keycloak.features.enabled.
  6. Update any custom wait-for-keycloak probe to target <release>-keycloak-metrics:9000.
  7. Validate locally with helm template charts/data-space-connector -f your-values.yaml and a one-off kc.sh import --dir=/opt/keycloak/data/import against a 26.6.3 pod before redeploying.
  8. Rerun your integration tests; confirm both consumer and provider Keycloaks reach Listening on http://0.0.0.0:8080 and that VC issuance flows complete.

For a worked end-to-end example, see the migrated k3s/consumer.yaml and k3s/provider.yaml overlays shipped with this release; the oid4vc-protocol-mappers.md reference now documents the 26.6.3 mapper API.

docs.title: Grafana Tempo Integration (10.2.0)
docs.text: 10.2.0 adds optional in-cluster Grafana Tempo trace storage and Grafana dashboard support, building on the OpenTelemetry tracing infrastructure introduced in 10.1.0. The integration is fully opt-in — no existing values are modified or removed.

docs.title: New optional subchart dependencies
docs.text:
Subchart Chart Version Repository tempo grafana/tempo 1.24.4 https://grafana.github.io/helm-charts grafana grafana/grafana 10.5.15 https://grafana.github.io/helm-charts

Both are disabled by default and gated by tempo.enabled / grafana.enabled.

docs.title: Auto-wired Collector → Tempo pipeline
docs.text:
When tracing.enabled=true and tempo.enabled=true, the chart renders a custom OTEL Collector ConfigMap (otel-collector-config-cm.yaml) that automatically injects an otlp/tempo exporter targeting the in-cluster Tempo gRPC endpoint. No manual Collector configuration is required — the existing opentelemetry-collector.config values are used as a base and the Tempo exporter is appended at render time.

When tempo.enabled=false, the ConfigMap renders the Collector configuration as-is (identical behaviour to 10.1.0).

docs.title: Auto-provisioned Grafana datasource
docs.text: When both grafana.enabled=true and tempo.enabled=true, the chart renders a datasource ConfigMap (grafana-tempo-datasource-cm.yaml) labelled grafana_datasource: "1". The Grafana sidecar picks it up automatically and registers Tempo as the default datasource. Operators can browse traces in the Grafana Explore view immediately after deployment.

docs.title: Enabling the full stack
docs.text:
tracing:
  enabled: true
tempo:
  enabled: true
grafana:
  enabled: true

This deploys: workloads with OTEL instrumentation → OTEL Collector → Grafana Tempo → Grafana dashboard. No additional configuration is needed for a working development/test setup.

docs.title: New values keys
docs.text: Key Type Default Description tempo.enabled bool false Toggle the bundled Grafana Tempo subchart tempo.tempo.retention string "48h" Trace retention period tempo.tempo.receivers.otlp.protocols.grpc.endpoint string "0.0.0.0:4317" OTLP gRPC listen address tempo.tempo.receivers.otlp.protocols.http.endpoint string "0.0.0.0:4318" OTLP HTTP listen address tempo.tempo.storage.trace.backend string "local" Storage backend (local, s3, gcs, azure) tempo.resources map cpu: 100m–500m, mem: 256Mi–1Gi Tempo pod resources grafana.enabled bool false Toggle the bundled Grafana subchart grafana.adminPassword string "admin" Grafana admin password (override in production) grafana.sidecar.datasources.enabled bool true Enable sidecar for auto-provisioning datasources grafana.sidecar.datasources.label string "grafana_datasource" Label the sidecar watches on ConfigMaps grafana.persistence.enabled bool false Enable persistent storage for Grafana grafana.resources map cpu: 100m–500m, mem: 128Mi–512Mi Grafana pod resources

docs.title: New template files
docs.text: File Purpose templates/otel-collector-config-cm.yaml Custom Collector ConfigMap with auto-injected Tempo exporter templates/grafana-tempo-datasource-cm.yaml Grafana datasource ConfigMap for Tempo

docs.title: New test file
docs.text: File Purpose tests/tempo_test.yaml Helm-unittest suite covering Collector ConfigMap and Grafana datasource rendering

docs.title: New helpers in _helpers.tpl
docs.text: Helper Returns dsc.tempo.endpoint http://<release>-tempo:4317 (Tempo OTLP gRPC endpoint for the Collector) dsc.tempo.queryEndpoint http://<release>-tempo:3200 (Tempo HTTP API endpoint for Grafana)

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Full documentation including architecture diagrams, quick-start guide, external Tempo usage, production considerations, and troubleshooting is available at Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry.

docs.title: No breaking changes
docs.text: This release is fully additive. All new subcharts default to enabled: false. Existing tracing behaviour from 10.1.0 is unchanged when Tempo and Grafana are not enabled.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Distributed Tracing (10.1.0)
docs.text:
10.1.0 adds optional end-to-end distributed tracing across the FIWARE Data Space Connector using OpenTelemetry. All first-party workloads (IdentityHub, fdsc-edc) and third-party subcharts that support native OTEL configuration (Keycloak, Scorpio, tm-forum-api, contract-management, marketplace) can export traces through the OTLP protocol to any compatible backend (Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, Honeycomb, etc.).

An optional OpenTelemetry Collector subchart is included for in-cluster trace aggregation and routing.

docs.title: Enabling tracing
docs.text:
Set tracing.enabled: true to inject OTEL_* environment variables into all supported workloads and enable the OpenTelemetry Java agent for IdentityHub:

tracing:
  enabled: true
  exporter:
    otlp:
      endpoint: ""          # defaults to the bundled collector
      protocol: "grpc"      # or "http/protobuf"
      insecure: true
  sampler: "parentbased_traceidratio"
  samplerArg: "1.0"
  propagators: "tracecontext,baggage"
  resourceAttributes: {}

opentelemetry-collector:
  enabled: true
